CI fails if a count INCREASES. Lower a number (never raise it) as debt is genuinely fixed, in a dedicated reviewed commit.

PB-011: this scalar total is NO LONGER the whole gate. A count-only ratchet is defeated by fixing one error and introducing a different one - the total holds and the build stays green while new debt lands (exactly how PB-005/PB-008 put 4 errors into this baseline unattributed). scripts/typecheck-certification-fingerprints.json now carries a PER-ERROR IDENTITY baseline - (file, TS code, normalized message) with a count per bucket - and scripts/typecheck-certification.js FAILS on any net-new identity even when this total is unchanged. The two artifacts must be regenerated together; the guard fails if their totals disagree.

PB-011: regenerate baselines ONLY via `npm run typecheck:certification:baseline`. It refuses to run under CI, refuses to RAISE a total, and refuses to absorb a net-new fingerprint unless --accept-new-debt is passed explicitly (which prints every absorbed fingerprint so it lands in the review record). Re-baselining is a governance act, never a build side effect.

Gaming this with blanket any / @ts-ignore / @ts-nocheck / excluding failing files is out of contract. The coverage assertion in scripts/typecheck-certification.js exists specifically so that dropping files from a project fails the check instead of lowering the count.
